page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-capable virtual machine belonging to the Lasv4 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core execution and multi-threaded decompression fall into the average category. The server exhibits notable bottlenecks in memory read bandwidth, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations scoring in the bottom 25%. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also register in the lower 25%, indicating potential performance limitations for highly transactional, memory-read-heavy workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L4as_v4 provides a dense combination of dedicated AMD EPYC processing, a relatively large memory allocation, and fast local NVMe storage without requiring high-tier compute pricing. The main tradeoff lies in its weak memory read bandwidth and lower database transaction scores despite the NVMe storage. This profile makes the server appropriate for memory-intensive general-purpose workloads, text processing, static web serving, and small-scale LLM inference tasks where write performance and local storage capacity are prioritized over raw memory read throughput.
